feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/public-sector CV with clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant platform/communications leadership. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited outcome-focused evidence beyond scope metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: progression at NACo shows increasing responsibility and supports the “senior digital leader” positioning.  
- Strong domain credibility: public-sector communications, Drupal modernization, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are consistently reinforced.  
- Good use of scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools improve credibility.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy / governance / workflows / content operations” appears often across summary, competencies, skills, and roles. Consolidate overlapping sections like Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT.  
- Add sharper impact/results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include measurable improvements such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption rates, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Fix style consistency issues: use one punctuation style for lists, standardize “organization-wide/organisation-wide” style, and remove minor inconsistencies like “social, and multimedia” (extra comma). No major misspellings found; grammar is strong overall.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning and clear seniority, but the intro is broad and repeats several ideas already covered in the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with sharper outcomes and a tighter focus on public-sector digital transformation.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language: “leading digital platform modernization, governance, and content operations.”
- Add 1–2 concrete scale signals from recent roles, e.g. “10,000+ page websites,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Tighten the second sentence to emphasize highest-value themes: web modernization, analytics, editorial governance, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers scalable digital platforms, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, and AI-enabled content discovery for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled content discovery” is more specific.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely repeats the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened into broader, differentiated capability areas with more parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use consistent noun phrases and reduce overlap: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership”
- Make the AI/technical item more specific and current: “AI-enabled search and structured content experiences” or “AI-enabled discovery and content systems”
- Tighten operational language: replace “Workflow automation and platform integration” with “Workflow automation and systems integration”
- Consider a sharper final version: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and systems integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several ideas already stated in the header, especially web modernization, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled experiences.
- Overlaps heavily with Topline Skills; keep this section higher-level and let later sections carry tools and detail.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense. Tightening wording and emphasizing outcomes or distinct scope will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing, and keep each item to one crisp line with parallel structure.
- Replace generic verbs like “Built”/“Developed” with more specific ones such as “Launched,” “Architected,” or “Produced.”
- Clarify scale or value where possible: audience, platform, campaign purpose, or business/public-sector impact.
- Standardize style: use “AI-enabled,” “Drupal 10,” and spell out “10 x 20-foot” consistently.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current freelance and NACo bullets; consider making the footer more portfolio-style with outcomes not stated elsewhere.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; use that as the model for adding unique context rather than restating responsibilities.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the opening, foreground the highest-impact work, and add outcomes or scale to distinguish it from your NACo entries.

Suggested edit
- Replace the generic opener with a sharper scope statement: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on digital strategy, Drupal platform improvement, content operations, and cross-channel governance.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets and lead with the most distinctive work:
- Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance models to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Designed Drupal-based campaign experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and member-facing resource/toolkit pages.
- Delivered CMS/front-end enhancements and troubleshooting for public-facing web properties; improved usability and content operations.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.
- Add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages/users, workflow time saved, search accuracy gains, engagement lifts, or publishing efficiency improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance,” “workflows,” and “Drupal/web improvement” overlap with NACo; keep this entry focused on consulting scope and the AI search initiative.
- Avoid repeating broad cross-channel leadership language already covered in your header and core competencies.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope-and-impact summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website transformation and make the result more outcome-focused: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen metrics where possible for channels/studio/analytics: add email list size, engagement growth, social growth, video output, event volume, reporting time saved, or adoption by leadership.
- Condense governance/operations into one results-oriented bullet: “Standardized publishing governance, editorial workflows, and cross-department planning to improve consistency, speed, and accountability.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version focused on leadership, scale, and business outcomes.
- Video studio/buildout may partially overlap with earlier multimedia bullets; emphasize that this was the first broadcast-quality in-house capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director of Digital Media role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing operational leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth before the larger strategic/platform ownership of the next role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and use stronger verbs: “Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.” Use “launched” only if accurate.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: newsletter open/click rates, video views, publishing turnaround time, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated, or growth in output/cadence.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video updates are also referenced in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the channel.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Make it sharper, more senior, and more clearly tied to recent enterprise-scale leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with more distinctive, senior wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for mission-driven organizations
- Editorial governance and cross-functional content operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Public-sector, membership, and advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy and planning
- If space allows, add one scale cue from recent work, e.g. “enterprise web ecosystems” or “large, multi-publisher environments.”
- Keep terminology consistent with recent roles: use “content operations” instead of “content planning” if you want stronger alignment with current consulting/NACo leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “multi-channel communications leadership” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a raw tool list rather than a curated topline summary. It also overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section, so this version should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities over exhaustive platform naming.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, API/workflow work.
- Consider dropping one or two lower-priority platforms here (for example WordPress or SharePoint) if they are already listed in Technical + IT.
- If accurate, sharpen with scope language: “enterprise Drupal environments,” “modular content systems,” or “cross-platform integrations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills more strategic and less exhaustive.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also echo Core Competencies; avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory rather than a value-focused skills line. Tighten it around analysis, reporting, and optimization outcomes, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Digital analytics & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with a stronger business phrase such as “executive dashboarding” or “decision-ready reporting”
- Clarify “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and content performance analysis” if accurate; it’s broader and more specific
- Possible rewrite: “Digital analytics & optimization — GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity; KPI framework design, executive dashboarding, and SEO/UX/content performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo bullet about expanding analytics infrastructure; avoid repeating the same wording
- BigQuery, GA4, Power BI, and Looker Studio are already evidenced in recent experience, so keep this section concise rather than restating impact here

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies plus multiple NACo bullets. Make it more specific to current/recent strengths and tools you can credibly defend.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Live Event Delivery**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and webinar production • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Hybrid/virtual event delivery • Post-production editing**
- If space allows, add one higher-value capability instead of a basic one: **Run-of-show and technical production planning** or **Speaker/remote presenter coordination**
- Keep wording parallel and outcome-oriented; avoid vague terms like “video production and editing” if you can specify format or environment.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This repeats **“Multimedia & live event production”** in Core Competencies; consider shortening one or removing that phrase from Core Competencies.
- “Studio operations” is already implied by your NACo studio achievement; don’t overstate it here unless supported by recent hands-on work.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but as written it adds little beyond the stronger “Topline Skills” section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize current/recent platforms or expanded slightly to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize the platforms most supported by recent roles: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages” and consider dropping “GitHub Pages” unless it was materially used in recent work.
- If space allows, add brief qualifiers to show depth: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages.”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use the same order and terminology wherever these platforms appear.
- If you want stronger impact, rename the line to “CMS Administration & Web Platforms” to better match your experience leading governance, migrations, and publishing operations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same tools plus broader capabilities.
- “Drupal” is already strongly evidenced in recent experience, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without adding context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around applied execution, not just languages: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group modern tooling separately: “Technical implementation & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope or use case tied to recent work: e.g., “for Drupal builds, campaign microsites, tagging, and workflow automation”
- Consider dropping version numbers unless relevant: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner than “HTML5 • CSS3”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, and workflow automation.
- To avoid repetition, keep this section tool-specific and let “Topline Skills” carry the broader capability framing.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a generic tool dump. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills, so it should emphasize systems-building tools over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Narrow to true automation/workflow platforms and separate project-management/chat tools if they must stay.
- Rewrite as: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello”  
- If space allows, add light grouping for clarity: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Workflow/project systems: Jira, Asana, Trello”
- If you’ve built meaningful automations, consider a stronger label: “Automation & Workflow Platforms” instead of “Systems”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same emphasis without adding specificity.
- Slack, Teams, and Basecamp are more collaboration tools than automation systems and dilute the section’s focus.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent roles, this line should emphasize platform fluency and campaign/engagement systems rather than repeat “email” generally.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, strengthen with functional context: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • newsletter operations, audience segmentation, campaign deployment**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was limited or older, consider dropping it to keep the list credible and current.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Your work experience already covers email/newsletter leadership extensively, so avoid adding generic phrases like “email campaigns” unless you specify a distinct technical capability.
- If Higher Logic or Mailchimp were not central in the 2022–present roles, this item may overstate recency unless reordered or trimmed.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item mostly repeats the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and reads like a generic keyword list. Tighten it to emphasize technical depth and optimization methods not already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Replace with a more specific list: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI dashboard development**
- Consider swapping **SEO** for **Google Search Console** or **technical SEO analysis** to make the skill more concrete and tool-/method-based.
- If space is tight, cut **Dashboarding** since reporting/dashboard capability is already implied by Power BI and Looker Studio.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; keep this version tool-focused and leave strategy/reporting language to the topline section.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid adding descriptive claims here unless they show distinct technical capability.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful early-career context, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more execution-focused and distinct from later leadership roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational build work and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add clearer action/result language: “Supported a major website refresh and improved cross-channel publishing workflows to streamline day-to-day digital communications.”
- Make multimedia more concrete: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates that expanded NACo’s recurring digital content capacity.”
- Tighten the management reference: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or remove if it feels minor.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” and “weekly video updates” overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on building the team and executing production.
- Avoid repeating leadership/governance themes already covered more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize the podcast launch and frame the rest as support to policy/program initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest achievement: “Supported innovation and research initiatives for NACo programs and policy teams, while expanding the organization’s early digital and multimedia communications.”
- Add the standout contribution as a second clause or bullet: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with specific outputs if known: web articles, audio segments, multimedia packages, research briefs, or stakeholder-facing materials.
- If possible, add scope: number of episodes, audiences served, teams supported, or projects coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; later entries better establish management and digital ownership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item is broad and partly overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and older podcast/video experience. Make it more tool-specific and senior-relevant, emphasizing production systems rather than generic creative software.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production Tools** or **Creative & Production Tools**
